title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
summary: Compartment epidemic models are often linear in coefficients that are physical parameters or products of parameters, so parameter estimation can be reduced to closed-form least squares. The paper introduces physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), which integrates the model in time with cubic-spline quadrature, avoids differentiating noisy data, estimates the initial state jointly, and is wrapped with split conformal prediction using simulated epidemics as the calibration population, plus a residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC). Across eleven DINN benchmarks, PIWR or PIR-FD6 is reported to improve on DINN errors by one to four orders of magnitude where sampling resolves the dynamics, each fit takes about a millisecond, and the 90% simultaneous intervals achieve 87–92% empirical coverage in all 88 tested settings.

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.split: 100 samples on [0,500] days; ε=0.01 noise level
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01
target.config_for_value: PIWR with cubic-spline quadrature and jointly estimated initial state; SIDR parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294; N=59·10^6; 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days; 1 % multiplicative Gaussian noise
target.est_compute: CPU, <1 s including data simulation; single PIWR fit is about 0.2 ms
target.quote: With 1 % noise the error of PIR-FD2 grows to 1.2–1.5 %, while PIR-FD6 and PIWR reach 0.12–0.49 %.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

claims.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01
claims.quote: With 1 % noise the error of PIR-FD2 grows to 1.2–1.5 %, while PIR-FD6 and PIWR reach 0.12–0.49 %.

claims.statement: Noise-free PIWR estimates α for the COVID-19 SIDR model with 0.000105 % relative error.

claims.quote: PIR-FD6 reduces it to 0.002–0.003 %, and PIWR to 0.0001 %, four orders of magnitude below DINN

claims.statement: PIWR is the most accurate estimator in 15 of the 22 model/noise settings across the eleven DINN benchmarks.
claims.table_ref: Section 5.4 and Table 3; statement over 22 model/noise settings
claims.quote: We find that PIWR is the most accurate estimator in 15 of the 22 model/noise settings, and PIR-FD6 in the remaining seven.

claims.statement: The plain split-conformal layer achieves mean 90.0 % empirical coverage over all 88 DINN benchmark settings, with a reported range of 87.6–92.0 %.
claims.table_ref: Section 5.5 coverage text and Fig. 5c; Table 4 reports PIWR-RACC coverage
claims.quote: the empirical coverage is 87.6–92.0 % for the plain layer (mean 90.0 %) and 86.7–92.5 % for the adaptive layer (mean 89.9 %).

claims.quote: With 1 % noise and γi known it is found that PIWR has the smallest median error, 0.51 % against 0.79–1.0 % for PIR-FD2/4/6

claims.table_ref: Table 6, row PIWR-VP, column test err. [%]
claims.quote: PIWR-VP reduces it to 7.6 %, and its intervals are 5–12 times narrower

claims.table_ref: Table 9, Case 3, row Rt, last 70 d, column PIWR

requirements.stmt: Formulate the epidemic model in parameter-linear form ẋ = f0(x,t) + A(x,t)θ, with the library A containing no unknown parameters and a map h recovering physical parameters from θ.
requirements.quote: the library A(x, t) ∈Rn×p contains no unknowns

requirements.stmt: For PIWR, use the integrated weak relation x(tj)=x0+Jjθ, with Jj the time integral of the library, instead of differentiating the data.
requirements.quote: The relation is still linear in θ, but it contains the data themselves instead of their derivatives.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate each library entry by a cubic spline with not-a-knot end conditions on the sample grid and integrate the spline exactly to obtain quadrature weights.
requirements.quote: interpolated over t0, . . . , tm−1 by a cubic spline (not-a-knot end conditions), and the spline is integrated exactly from t0 to tj.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the initial state x0 jointly with θ using the augmented system with identity blocks for x0.
requirements.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns, so that the noise of the first sample is not propagated into every equation.

requirements.stmt: Solve the PIWR least-squares problem by a numerically stable orthogonal factorization or SVD-based least squares, not by explicitly forming the normal equations.
requirements.quote: In implementation, we do not form the normal equations (16), whose condition number is the square of that of MD.

requirements.stmt: Column-scale the regression matrix to unit column norm before the solve; scaling is a change of variables and leaves the minimizer unchanged.
requirements.cite: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, equations (11) and implementation after (18)
requirements.quote: the columns are scaled to unit norm before the solve

requirements.stmt: For the synthetic benchmarks, add compartment-wise noise with standard deviation ε times the maximum absolute true compartment value over the time grid.
requirements.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

requirements.stmt: For conformal calibration, draw calibration parameters from a prior box of ±50 % around literature values, capped at 1 for probabilities and [0,c] for parameters whose literature value is zero.
requirements.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

requirements.stmt: Use the maximum normalized error over all parameters as the split-conformal nonconformity score, then form simultaneous intervals with the corresponding quantile.
requirements.quote: To obtain intervals that hold for all k parameters at once, we use the maximum normalized error as the nonconformity score

requirements.stmt: For PIWR-RACC, compute the residual-adaptive factor h = 1 + R/Rbar, with Rbar the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and apply h to scores and intervals.
requirements.quote: with  ̄R the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and use it in the score (20) and the intervals (21).

requirements.stmt: Use 999 calibration problems and α=0.1 for the 90 % simultaneous intervals, with tuning done on separate draws.
requirements.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1.

requirements.stmt: Recover physical parameters through ω=h(θ) and, when uncertainty in ω is reported, propagate the coefficient covariance by the delta method.
requirements.quote: The physical parameters are ˆω = h(ˆθ). Their uncertainty follows from the delta method

requirements.stmt: For the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark, use N=59·10^6, initial state S0=N−1 and I0=1, parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days.
requirements.cite: Section 2 worked example and Appendix A.1
requirements.quote: 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days (∆t = 5.05 days) of the solution with (α, β, γ) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294)

requirements.stmt: Report errors as percent of the actual parameter value, using the median over estimated parameters of a model when summarizing a model.
requirements.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

requirements.stmt: Generate synthetic benchmark trajectories with LSODA at relative and absolute tolerances of 10^-10.
requirements.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not give the random seed or specify whether the Table 2 PIWR value 0.124 % is from one noise realization, a median over realizations, or a repeated-fit median.
assumptions.chosen: Use a single fixed-seed realization for the point estimate, then check stability over 1,000 realizations at the literature values.
assumptions.quote: for ε = 1 %, on 1,000 noise realizations at the literature values.

assumptions.gap: The paper says row scaling is selected per model on tuning draws but does not state whether the SIDR PIWR run uses Dn=In or compartment-max scaling.
assumptions.chosen: Use Dn=In for SIDR unless a separate tuning run on 100 draws says otherwise.
assumptions.quote: whether to use it (Dn = In otherwise) is decided per model and estimator on a tuning set (section 5.1).

assumptions.gap: The exact definition of the reported single-parameter % error for α is not given beyond the general metric sentence.
assumptions.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

assumptions.gap: The initial state x0 is estimated jointly but the paper does not state whether positivity or bounds are imposed on x0.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained least squares, as in the augmented linear system.
assumptions.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns

assumptions.gap: The exact ODE solver tolerances for the synthetic SIDR data generation are not stated in the main text.
assumptions.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The printed Δt=5.05 days is rounded; the exact grid construction is not shown.
The population is printed as 59·10^6 in OCR text; the exact integer is not otherwise specified.
The paper does not say whether any smoothing is applied to noisy states before evaluating the library inside the PIWR integrals.
assumptions.chosen: No smoothing; use noisy states directly in the library and integrate by spline.
assumptions.quote: Both PIR and PIWR evaluate the library at the noisy samples.

assumptions.gap: The least-squares rank-deficiency threshold and exact SVD/LAPACK routine are not specified.
assumptions.chosen: numpy.linalg.lstsq with default rcond in float64.

assumptions.gap: The exact joint prior box for α, β, γ in the SIDR calibration is not tabulated parameter by parameter.
assumptions.chosen: Independent uniform [0.5α*,1.5α*], [0.5β*,1.5β*], [0.5γ*,1.5γ*], with no cap binding since all values are below 1.
assumptions.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

assumptions.gap: The random seeds for the 100 row-scaling tuning draws and 200 Rbar tuning draws are not given.
assumptions.chosen: Use separate fixed seeds for row-scaling tuning, Rbar tuning, calibration, and testing.
assumptions.quote: Every estimator is tuned on draws that are not used for calibration or testing: the row scaling on 100 draws,  ̄R on 200 draws.

assumptions.gap: The seed splitting for 999 calibration problems and 2,000 test problems is not specified.
assumptions.chosen: Use fixed seed 0 and disjoint generated pools for calibration and testing.
assumptions.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1. The coverage is measured on 2,000 independent test problems

assumptions.gap: Whether coverage is evaluated for all parameters simultaneously or marginally is not fully explicit in the table rows.
assumptions.chosen: Use simultaneous coverage of all parameters in the model, matching the conformal score.

assumptions.gap: The numerical precision and implementation language for the least-squares solve are not part of the mathematical method but affect exact values.
assumptions.quote: all estimates are dense least-squares solves (numpy.linalg.lstsq) in double precision.

assumptions.gap: Whether the RACC h factor is used for the point estimate or only for interval widths is not explicit in the score formula text.
assumptions.chosen: Apply h only to scores and interval widths; point estimate remains the PIWR least-squares estimate.
assumptions.quote: Scaling the conformal scores and intervals by a factor that increases with this residual widens the intervals for difficult data sets and narrows them for easy ones

assumptions.gap: The paper does not state whether the first and last samples are included in the PIWR linear system beyond saying all samples are used.
assumptions.chosen: Include all m samples, with J0=0 and the measured x0 on the right-hand side.
assumptions.quote: uses all samples, including the end points

assumptions.gap: The paper does not constrain the SIDR parameter estimates to be positive or within a physical range.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained linear least squares for the point estimate.
assumptions.quote: PIR and PIWR search an unbounded parameter space

assumptions.gap: The noise scale uses the maximum true compartment value, but the paper does not state whether that maximum is computed before or after adding noise.
assumptions.chosen: Maximum of the true noise-free trajectory per compartment.
assumptions.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

why: The only linked repository (Shaier/DINN) is the *baseline* the paper benchmarks against, not the paper's own method: it contains 626 files of Jupyter notebooks and CSVs for DINN training, zero Python modules, and no PIWR / PIR-FD / conformal-prediction code at all. The paper's contribution (physics-informed weak regression: integrate the linear-in-parameters SIDR equations in time with cubic-spline quadrature, solve a closed-form least-squares problem with the initial state as a free unknown) exists only as a mathematical description in the text, so it must be reimplemented. The repo is still useful in one narrow way: Diseases/COVID/generate_covid_data.ipynb and sidr.csv pin down the exact SIDR benchmark (N = 59e6, S0 = N-1, I0 = 1, alpha = 0.191, beta = 0.05, gamma = 0.0294, 100 points on [0,500], 1% multiplicative noise), which is the match target for C1, and the data can equally be regenerated from Appendix A.1 alone. The reimplementation is cheap: a 4-state linear ODE system, a cumulative-spline quadrature matrix, and one numpy.linalg.lstsq call.
est_runtime: 5-10 minutes of command time: ~1 min to install numpy/scipy/matplotlib, ~10 s to simulate the SIDR benchmark, milliseconds per PIWR fit, so a few hundred repeated fits plus a noise-level sweep finish in seconds; the remainder is development of the ~200-line weak-form estimator and the clean re-run.
blockers: The linked repository is the DINN baseline (PyTorch 1.8.1, pandas 1.1.5, numpy 1.19.2, Python 3.6) — the paper's own estimator is not in it, so nothing in the repo produces any of the claimed numbers

requirements.txt pins torch/numpy versions that will not install cleanly on this machine's Python 3.12, but that is moot since the DINN baseline is the comparison method and not needed for the match target
No scripts, only notebooks; no CLI entrypoint that emits a target number

The two runs reported for C1 are single noise realizations implicitly (no seed stated), so an exact 0.124% match requires reproducing the same random draw; honest reproduction should report median/mean over realizations and accept a small deviation

approach: Reimplement PIWR for the SIDR benchmark directly from the equations: generate the true trajectory with LSODA at 1e-10 tolerances, and for C1 use the 100-point DINN `sidr.csv` 1% benchmark when available (falling back to a fixed-seed regeneration from Appendix A.1) so the single noise realisation is not invented. For each compartment and each library column, evaluate A(x,t) on the sample grid, interpolate with a not-a-knot cubic spline, integrate the spline exactly to every sample time, and assemble the augmented linear system with x0 as four extra unknowns. Solve the column-normalised system with `numpy.linalg.lstsq` (never forming normal equations), unscale, extract theta=(alpha,beta,gamma), and compute |alpha_hat-0.191|/0.191*100. Add noiseless, stability-over-realizations, and timing checks, then write all numbers to `results/metrics.json`.
steps: Create `config.py` with the exact SIDR parameters, time grid, noise level, LSODA tolerances, spline/quadrature settings, column scaling, lstsq settings, target and tolerance; do not install DINN requirements or run DINN notebooks.
Implement `src/sidr.py`: SIDR RHS with state order [S,I,D,R], LSODA simulation at rtol=atol=1e-10, compartment-wise Gaussian noise per R7, and a flexible CSV loader for the DINN `sidr.csv` benchmark.

Load `Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv` if present; inspect header/columns and confirm there are 100 rows with time plus S,I,D,R. Compare it with a noiseless LSODA trajectory to verify it is the 1% noise file. If it is missing or not the 1% file, use `Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv`; if no candidate CSV exists, regenerate with seed 0.

Implement `src/piwr.py`: for each state c and each library column k, evaluate A_{c,k}(x_noisy(t_i),t_i) on the sample grid, build a not-a-knot CubicSpline, integrate exactly from t_0 to every t_j via the spline antiderivative, and store J[c][j,k].

Build the augmented system M and RHS y: for each state c and time j, set M[row,c]=1 for x0_c and M[row,n_states+k]=J[c][j,k] for theta_k; set y[row]=x_noisy[j,c]. Include all m samples and ensure J[:,0]=0 at j=0.

Column-scale M to unit column norms, solve with `numpy.linalg.lstsq(M_scaled,y,rcond=None)` in float64, unscale coefficients by dividing by the column norms, and extract x0_hat and theta_hat=(alpha_hat,beta_hat,gamma_hat).

Run the noiseless sanity fit on the true trajectory: verify alpha_hat is within about 1e-4% of 0.191 and x0_hat matches the true initial state; if not, debug the SIDR library, spline integration, or state/column mapping before touching the 1% data.
Run the C1 fit on the verified 1% benchmark CSV: compute alpha_hat and `100*abs(alpha_hat-0.191)/0.191`; record whether it lies in [0.1116,0.1364].
Run the stability sweep: regenerate 1000 independent 1% noise realisations with fixed seeds, fit each with PIWR, and store median, mean, IQR and 5–95% range of the alpha percent error.
Run the timing check: repeat the PIWR fit 30 times on the C1 data set and record median CPU milliseconds per fit.

Write `results/metrics.json` with the C1 headline fields (alpha_true, alpha_hat, alpha_rel_error_pct, target_pct, within_tolerance), data source, matrix shape/rank/condition number, x0_hat, beta_hat, gamma_hat, noiseless check, stability summary, timing summary, and the exact config used.

Validate the JSON by re-reading it and printing a summary; verify the headline error is compared against the relative tolerance band and that the noiseless, stability and timing diagnostics are present.
smoke_test: Implement a `--smoke` mode in `reproduce.py` that loads/simulates the SIDR benchmark once, builds M, asserts M.shape==(400,7), asserts J_0==0, checks rank(M_scaled)==7, and runs two fits: (i) noiseless true states, expected alpha error below 1e-4%, and (ii) one noisy 1% realisation, expected alpha error in the 0.05–1% range. This proves the spline quadrature, augmented least squares, scaling, and alpha extraction without the 1000-realisation sweep.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: t has shape (100,), X_noisy has shape (100,4), all finite; time runs from 0 to 500 inclusive with `np.linspace(0,500,100)`.
True trajectory sanity: S decreases from N-1, I starts at 1 and peaks, D and R are nonnegative and nondecreasing; max absolute value per compartment is nonzero so the R7 noise scale is well defined.

Noise sanity on the benchmark CSV: if using `sidr.csv`, compare it with the noiseless trajectory and verify residuals are approximately N(0, (0.01*max|x_c|)^2); if not, select the correct 100-point 1% noise CSV before fitting.
Matrix sanity: M has shape (4*100,4+3)=(400,7); J at t_0 is exactly zero for every column; after unit-column scaling no column has zero norm; rank is 7 and the scaled condition number is reported.

Noiseless baseline: a PIWR fit to the true states recovers alpha to near machine/quadrature accuracy (target <1e-4% relative error) and gives x0 close to [N-1,1,0,0]; failure here means an equation/library/quadrature bug, not a noise issue.
Single noisy fit sanity: alpha_hat is positive and within a few percent of 0.191; the reported C1 error should be near the paper's 0.124%, not orders of magnitude larger.
Timing sanity: 30 repeated fits on the 100-point SIDR problem should be milliseconds or less on CPU; if a fit takes seconds, the implementation is rebuilding splines or solving the wrong problem.
budget_plan: About 10 minutes of command time: 2 min creating `config.py`, `src/sidr.py`, `src/piwr.py`, `src/evaluate.py`, and `reproduce.py`; 2 min on smoke/noiseless validation and fixing any shape or quadrature bug; 3 min on the C1 fit plus the 1000-realisation stability sweep (each fit is sub-millisecond to millisecond, so the sweep is dominated by data generation and Python overhead); 1 min for the 30-repeat timing check; 2 min for writing, re-reading, and validating `results/metrics.json`.

# Initial conditions
N = 59e6

S0 = N - 1
I0 = 1
D0 = 0
R0 = 0
# A grid of time points (in days)
t = np.linspace(0, 500, 100) 

#parameters
alpha = 0.191
beta = 0.05
gamma = 0.0294

# The SIR model differential equations.
def deriv(y, t, alpha, betta, gamma):
    S, I, D, R = y
    dSdt = - (alpha / N) * S * I
    dIdt = (alpha / N) * S * I - beta * I - gamma * I 
    dDdt = gamma * I
    dRdt = beta * I

    return dSdt, dIdt, dDdt, dRdt


# Initial conditions vector
y0 = S0, I0, D0, R0
# Integrate the SIR equations over the time grid, t.

S, I, D, R = ret.T

Abstract
Compartment models of infectious diseases are often linear in a vector of coefficients, each
of which is a physical parameter or a product or ratio of parameters. We exploit this by
using closed-form least squares, and equip the estimates with distribution-free uncertainty.
Physics-informed regression (PIR) fits the parameters to finite-difference estimates of the time
derivatives. We introduce a new physics-informed weak regression (PIWR) method, which
integrates the model in time instead, contains no derivatives of the data, estimates the initial
state jointly, and is high-order accurate with cubic-spline quadrature. To quantify uncertainty
we wrap both estimators in split conformal prediction. The calibration population is generated
by the physics-based model itself: epidemics with known parameters are simulated, perturbed
with the data’s noise model and processed by the same fixed estimator. This yields intervals
for all parameters of a model at once with a finite-sample coverage guarantee. A residual-
adaptive factor, computed without ground truth, scales the uncertainty intervals of each
data set. With PIWR we call the new conformalized approach PIWR-RACC. On all eleven
benchmark models of disease-informed neural networks (DINNs), from a four-state SIDR
model of COVID-19 to a nine-state host–vector model of Zika, PIWR is the most accurate
estimator in 15 of 22 model/noise settings. Where the sampling resolves the dynamics,
PIWR or sixth-order finite-difference-based PIR-FD6 is one to four orders of magnitude more

"""Configuration for the PIWR reproduction of the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark.

Single source of truth for every number used by reproduce.py.  All values are
taken from the paper (arXiv:2610.19058):
  * Section 2 worked example / Appendix A.1 (eq. 28-29): SIDR model, parameters,
    initial state, N, time grid.
  * Section 3.2 (eq. 12-18): PIWR weak form, cubic-spline quadrature, augmented
    system with x0 as extra unknowns, column scaling, least-squares solve.
  * Section 5.1 (setup): compartment-wise noise model, error metric.
  * Appendix A: LSODA at rtol = atol = 1e-10.
"""

import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths
WORKSPACE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_DIR = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "repo")
DINN_SIDR_CSV = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "Diseases", "COVID", "sidr.csv")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "results")
METRICS_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "metrics.json")

# ------------------------------------------------- SIDR model (R13 / A.1)
POPULATION_N = 59.0e6
STATE_NAMES = ("S", "I", "D", "R")
N_STATES = 4
PARAM_NAMES = ("alpha", "beta", "gamma")
TRUE_PARAMS = {"alpha": 0.191, "beta": 0.05, "gamma": 0.0294}
TRUE_X0 = (POPULATION_N - 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)  # (N-1, 1, 0, 0)

# time grid: 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days
N_SAMPLES = 100
T_END = 500.0

# ------------------------------------------------------------ solver (R15)
SOLVER_METHOD = "LSODA"
SOLVER_RTOL = 1e-10
SOLVER_ATOL = 1e-10

# ------------------------------------------------------------- noise (R7)
NOISE_EPSILON = 0.01  # 1 % multiplicative Gaussian noise

# ------------------------------------------------------- PIWR settings
# R3: not-a-knot cubic spline, integrated exactly from t0 to tj
SPLINE_BC_TYPE = "not-a-knot"
# R4: initial state estimated jointly as n extra unknowns (identity block)
JOINT_INITIAL_STATE = True
# R6: columns scaled to unit norm before the solve
COLUMN_SCALING = True
# R5: SVD-based least squares (numpy.linalg.lstsq), never the normal equations
LEAST_SQUARES = "numpy.linalg.lstsq"
# Optional row scaling by compartment magnitude (section 3.2, after eq. 14).
# The paper calls it optional and tunes it on 100 draws; we evaluate both and
# report the choice used for the headline number.
ROW_SCALING = False

# ------------------------------------------------------------ evaluation
ERROR_METRIC = "100 * abs(hat_omega - omega) / omega"  # R14
STABILITY_REALIZATIONS = 1000  # section 5.1: 1,000 noise realizations
TIMING_REPEATS = 30  # Table 2: median of 30 repeated fits
POINT_ESTIMATE_SEED = 0  # fixed seed for the single reported noise draw

# --------------------------------------------------------------- target
# Paper Table 2 / Table 10, row alpha, column PIWR, noise level eps = 0.01.
TARGET_ALPHA_PCT_ERROR = 0.124
TOLERANCE_RELATIVE = 0.10  # acceptance band: +/-10 % relative
TOLERANCE_BAND = (
    TARGET_ALPHA_PCT_ERROR * (1.0 - TOLERANCE_RELATIVE),
    TARGET_ALPHA_PCT_ERROR * (1.0 + TOLERANCE_RELATIVE),
)

"""SIDR benchmark: dynamics, LSODA simulation, noise, library, data loading.

Model (paper eq. 5 / eq. 28), state order x = (S, I, D, R):

    dS/dt = -alpha * S * I / N
    dI/dt =  alpha * S * I / N - (beta + gamma) * I
    dD/dt =  gamma * I
    dR/dt =  beta * I

with theta = (alpha, beta, gamma) and the library

    A(x, t) = [[ -S*I/N,  0,      0    ],
               [  S*I/N, -I,     -I    ],
               [  0,      0,      I    ],
               [  0,      I,      0    ]]
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

import config as C


def sidr_rhs(t, y, alpha, beta, gamma, N):
    """Right-hand side of the SIDR system (eq. 28)."""
    S, I, D, R = y
    a = alpha * S * I / N
    return np.array([
        -a,
        a - (beta + gamma) * I,
        gamma * I,
        beta * I,
    ])


def simulate(t, params=None, x0=None):
    """Integrate the SIDR model with LSODA at rtol = atol = 1e-10 (R15).

    Returns an (m, 4) array of the true states at the sample times ``t``.
    """
    params = C.TRUE_PARAMS if params is None else params
    x0 = C.TRUE_X0 if x0 is None else np.asarray(x0, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    sol = solve_ivp(
        sidr_rhs,
        (t[0], t[-1]),
        x0,
        method=C.SOLVER_METHOD,
        rtol=C.SOLVER_RTOL,
        atol=C.SOLVER_ATOL,
        t_eval=t,
        args=(params["alpha"], params["beta"], params["gamma"], C.POPULATION_N),
    )
    if not sol.success:
        raise RuntimeError("LSODA integration failed: " + sol.message)
    return sol.y.T


def library(X, N=None):
    """Evaluate A(x, t) at the sampled states.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : (m, 4) array of states (noisy or true).

    Returns
    -------
    A : (m, n_states, p) array with A[i, r, c] = A_{r,c}(x(t_i), t_i).
    """
    N = C.POPULATION_N if N is None else N
    X = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(X, dtype=float))
    S, I = X[:, 0], X[:, 1]
    m = X.shape[0]
    A = np.zeros((m, C.N_STATES, 3))

"""Physics-informed weak regression (PIWR) for the SIDR benchmark.

Implements the paper's section 3.2:

  eq. (12)  x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta,  J_j = int_{t0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds
  eq. (13)  cubic-spline (not-a-knot) quadrature with grid-only weights w_ji
  eq. (14)  augmented system M z ~ y with x0 as n extra unknowns
  eq. (15)  least-squares minimisation of the residual
  eq. (11)  unit column-norm scaling before the solve
  eq. (16)  solved by SVD least squares, never by forming the normal equations
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

import config as C

_WEIGHT_CACHE = {}


def quadrature_weights(t):
    """Weight matrix W with J_j = sum_i W[j, i] * A_i (eq. 13).

    Every library entry is interpolated by a not-a-knot cubic spline over the
    sample grid and the spline is integrated *exactly* from t0 to t_j.  Because
    the spline is linear in its data, the antiderivative at t_j is a linear
    combination of the sampled values, so the weights depend only on the grid
    and are computed once.  W[0, :] is exactly zero (J_0 = 0).
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    key = (t.shape, float(t[0]), float(t[-1]), C.SPLINE_BC_TYPE)
    if key in _WEIGHT_CACHE:
        return _WEIGHT_CACHE[key]
    m = t.size
    W = np.zeros((m, m))
    for i in range(m):
        e = np.zeros(m)
        e[i] = 1.0
        spl = CubicSpline(t, e, bc_type=C.SPLINE_BC_TYPE, axis=0)
        anti = spl.antiderivative()
        W[:, i] = anti(t)
    # kill round-off in the first row so that J_0 is exactly zero
    W[0, :] = 0.0
    _WEIGHT_CACHE[key] = W
    return W


def integrated_library(A, W):
    """J[j, r, c] = int_{t0}^{t_j} A_{r,c}(x(s), s) ds via the spline weights."""
    return np.einsum("ji,irc->jrc", W, A)


def build_system(X, W, row_scaling=None):
    """Assemble the augmented system M z ~ y (eq. 14).

    M has nm rows and (p + n) columns; the first n columns are the identity
    block for x0, the remaining p columns hold J_j.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m, n = X.shape
    A = _library_of(X)
    J = integrated_library(A, W)          # (m, n, p)
    p = J.shape[2]
    M = np.zeros((m * n, n + p))
    for j in range(m):
        sl = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
        M[sl, :n] = np.eye(n)
        M[sl, n:] = J[j]
    y = X.reshape(-1)
    if row_scaling is not None:
        d = np.repeat(np.asarray(row_scaling, dtype=float), m)
        M = M * d[:, None]
        y = y * d
    return M, y, J


def _library_of(X):
    from src.sidr import library
    return library(X)


def solve(M, y, column_scaling=True):
    """Column-scaled SVD least squares (eq. 11, 16); no normal equations."""
    M = np.asarray(M, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if column_scaling:
        norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
        if np.any(norms == 0.0):
            raise np.linalg.LinAlgError("zero-norm column in the regression matrix")
        Ms = M / norms[None, :]
    else:
        norms = np.ones(M.shape[1])
        Ms = M
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Ms, y, rcond=None)
    z = coef / norms
    resid = y - Ms @ coef
    rank = np.linalg.matrix_rank(Ms)
    cond = np.linalg.cond(Ms)
    return z, {"rank": int(rank), "cond_scaled": float(cond),
               "residual_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(resid)),
               "rel_residual": float(np.linalg.norm(resid) / np.linalg.norm(y))}


def fit(X, t=None, row_scaling=None, column_scaling=True, return_system=False):
    """Run one PIWR fit on the sampled states ``X`` (m, n).

    Returns a dict with theta_hat, x0_hat, diagnostics.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m, n = X.shape
    t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, m) if t is None else np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    W = quadrature_weights(t)
    M, y, J = build_system(X, W, row_scaling=row_scaling)
    z, info = solve(M, y, column_scaling=column_scaling)
    p = J.shape[2]
    out = {
        "theta_hat": z[:p],
        "x0_hat": z[p:],
        "J": J,
        "M": M,
        "info": info,
    }
    if return_system:
        out["y"] = y
    return out


def compartment_row_scales(X):
    """s_c = max_i |x~_{i,c}| (optional row scaling, section 3.2)."""
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    return np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)

import numpy as np

import config as C

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)

# --- verify the quadrature weights against direct spline integration
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

A = sidr.library(X)
W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)
Jw = piwr.integrated_library(A, W)
Jd = np.zeros_like(Jw)
for r in range(C.N_STATES):
    for c in range(3):
        spl = CubicSpline(t, A[:, r, c], bc_type="not-a-knot")
        anti = spl.antiderivative()
        Jd[:, r, c] = anti(t) - anti(t[0])

4
Conformal prediction with physics-based models
4.1
A calibration population from the model
Split conformal prediction (Vovk et al., 2005; Lei et al., 2018; Angelopoulos and Bates, 2023) requires
calibration examples with known truth that are exchangeable with the test case. In standard regression
these are held-out data points. A model coefficient has no such examples: each data set has exactly one
true parameter vector, and calibrating |ˆωj −ωj| requires a population of data sets with different known
parameters. For a physics-based model this population is cheap to generate, and generating it is the central
idea of our extension. Let D be a prior box for the parameters. For i = 1, . . . , n:
1. draw ω(i) ∼U(D);
2. simulate the model from the same initial condition on the same time grid as the data;
3. add noise with the same noise model as the data;
4. run the fixed estimator (PIR or PIWR, with the same settings) to obtain ˆω(i) and ˆσ(i).
The estimator is never refitted. All of its tuning (finite-difference order, row scaling, reference residual) is
done on separate tuning draws, so that the calibration scores stay exchangeable with the score of a new
problem from the same population.

Bechmarks across all eleven models
We compare the results of the physics-informed regression models in Table 3 and fig. 4 summarize the accuracy
for all models. We find that PIWR is the most accurate estimator in 15 of the 22 model/noise settings,
and PIR-FD6 in the remaining seven. Without noise, PIWR or PIR-FD6 improves on the reported DINN
errors by one to four orders of magnitude for COVID-19, Ebola, Dengue, Pneumonia, Polio and Tuberculosis,
is comparable for HIV and Zika, and less accurate for Smallpox (6.9 % against 5.1 %) and Measles (9.4 %
against 3.4 %).
With 1 % noise the advantage of PIWR is largest where the finite differences amplify the noise of small
compartments: Pneumonia (11 % against 13–57 %), Ebola (25 % against 37–40 %), Measles (28 % against

84–88 %) and HIV (22 % against 35–51 %).
Two benchmarks remain out of reach at their DINN sampling. Anthrax has outbreaks of a few days, sampled
every 40 days, and all estimators have median errors of 7–85 %. For Zika, the row scaling selected on the
tuning draws for PIWR is suboptimal for the literature case (6.3 % against 0.19 % for PIR-FD6 without
noise).
The DINN errors are not directly comparable. Shaier et al. (2022) restrict every parameter to a search range
that is typically ±1–10 % around the literature value, which bounds their errors by construction. They also
report estimates for parameters that do not occur in the equations (k, τ, λv, m) or that cannot be separated
from others (μT and N, c, θ1, δ1, δ2, a; table 1). PIR and PIWR search an unbounded parameter space, and
the least-squares structure makes identifiability explicit as collinear columns of the library.

import glob
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
import config as C
from src import sidr

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
scale = 0.01 * np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)
print("expected 1% noise std:", scale)

for f in sorted(glob.glob("repo/**/*.csv", recursive=True)):
    if "csse" in f:
        continue
    try:
        d = np.genfromtxt(f, delimiter=",")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f, "ERR", e)
        continue
    if d.ndim != 2:
        print(f"{f}: shape {d.shape} (not 2d)")
        continue
    # find orientation with 100 columns
    cand = None
    if d.shape[1] == 100 and d.shape[0] in (4, 5):
        cand = ("rows=states", d[1:].T if d.shape[0] == 5 else d.T, d[0])
    elif d.shape[0] == 100 and d.shape[1] in (4, 5):
        cand = ("cols=states", d[:, 1:] if d.shape[1] == 5 else d, d[:, 0])
    if cand is None:
        print(f"{f}: shape {d.shape} -> skip")
        continue
    orient, Xc, tc = cand
    if Xc.shape[1] != 4 or not np.allclose(tc, t, atol=1e-6):
        print(f"{f}: shape {d.shape} orient={orient} t-mismatch")
        continue
    r = Xc - X
    print(f"{f}: orient={orient} resid std={np.round(r.std(axis=0),1)} "
          f"ratio_to_1pct={np.round(r.std(axis=0)/scale,3)}")

"""Diagnosis: is the PIWR alpha estimate statistically efficient at 1% noise?

For each noise realization we compare the empirical error |alpha_hat - alpha|
with the least-squares-predicted standard error sigma_alpha taken from the
theta-block of sigma_bar^2 (M^T M)^{-1} (paper eqs. 17 and 19).
"""

import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import piwr, sidr

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
true = np.array([C.TRUE_PARAMS["alpha"], C.TRUE_PARAMS["beta"], C.TRUE_PARAMS["gamma"]])
W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)


def fit_with_cov(Xn, rows=None):
    """PIWR fit plus the theta-block of sigma_bar^2 (M^T M)^{-1}."""
    m, n = Xn.shape
    M, y, J = piwr.build_system(Xn, W)
    if rows is not None:
        M = M[rows]
        y = y[rows]
    z, info = piwr.solve(M, y)
    theta = z[n:]
    r = y - M @ z
    dof = M.shape[0] - M.shape[1]
    s2 = float(r @ r) / dof
    MtM_inv = np.linalg.inv(M.T @ M)
    cov = s2 * MtM_inv
    se = np.sqrt(np.diag(cov))
    return theta, se[n:], info, s2


def block_rows(which):
    """Row indices of the S-block (compartment 0) or I-block (compartment 1)."""
    m = C.N_SAMPLES
    c = 0 if which == "S" else 1
    return np.array([j * C.N_STATES + c for j in range(m)])


N = 200
rng = np.random.default_rng(2024)
err_a = np.zeros(N)
se_a = np.zeros(N)
err_b = np.zeros(N)
se_b = np.zeros(N)
err_g = np.zeros(N)
se_g = np.zeros(N)
s_only = np.zeros(N)
i_only = np.zeros(N)

for k in range(N):
    Xn = sidr.add_noise(X, C.NOISE_EPSILON, rng)
    th, se, info, s2 = fit_with_cov(Xn)
    err_a[k] = th[0] - true[0]
    se_a[k] = se[0]
    err_b[k] = th[1] - true[1]
    se_b[k] = se[1]
    err_g[k] = th[2] - true[2]
    se_g[k] = se[2]
    thS, _, _, _ = fit_with_cov(Xn, rows=block_rows("S"))
    thI, _, _, _ = fit_with_cov(Xn, rows=block_rows("I"))
    s_only[k] = 100 * abs(thS[0] - true[0]) / true[0]
    i_only[k] = 100 * abs(thI[0] - true[0]) / true[0]

print("=== full PIWR, %d realizations ===" % N)
print("alpha: empirical std of signed error = %.6e" % err_a.std())
print("alpha: mean predicted SE             = %.6e" % se_a.mean())
print("alpha: ratio empirical/predicted     = %.3f" % (err_a.std() / se_a.mean()))
print("alpha: mean |err|/SE                 = %.3f" % np.mean(np.abs(err_a) / se_a))
print("beta : ratio empirical/predicted     = %.3f" % (err_b.std() / se_b.mean()))
print("gamma: ratio empirical/predicted     = %.3f" % (err_g.std() / se_g.mean()))
print()
print("alpha %% error: median %.4f  mean %.4f  q10 %.4f  q90 %.4f"
      % (np.median(100*np.abs(err_a)/true[0]), np.mean(100*np.abs(err_a)/true[0]),
         np.percentile(100*np.abs(err_a)/true[0], 10), np.percentile(100*np.abs(err_a)/true[0], 90)))
print("S-block only : alpha %% error median %.4f" % np.median(s_only))
print("I-block only : alpha %% error median %.4f" % np.median(i_only))
print()
print("signed alpha error: mean %.3e  std %.3e" % (err_a.mean(), err_a.std()))
print("signed beta  error: mean %.3e  std %.3e" % (err_b.mean(), err_b.std()))
print("signed gamma error: mean %.3e  std %.3e" % (err_g.mean(), err_g.std()))

"""Audit the effective noise level of every SIDR csv in the DINN repo.

For each candidate file we compute, per compartment,
    std(csv - noiseless LSODA trajectory) / max_t |true trajectory|
which must equal epsilon = 0.01 for a 1 % noise file (R7) and ~1e-7 for a
noise-free file.
"""

import glob
import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import sidr

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
cmax = np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)
print("max|true| per compartment:", cmax)
print("1 % of that (R7 noise std):", 0.01 * cmax)
print()

files = [
    "repo/Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/param_ranges/sidr_100_pts.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/different_architectures/covid_100_pts.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/learning_rates/covid_100_pts.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/missing_data/covid_100_pts.csv",
    "repo/COVID_Tutorial.csv",
]
for f in files:
    d = np.genfromtxt(f, delimiter=",")
    Xc = d[1:].T
    r = Xc - X
    ratio = r.std(axis=0) / cmax
    print(f"{f}")
    print(f"    shape={d.shape}  t matches grid: {np.allclose(d[0], t)}")
    print(f"    std(csv-true)      = {r.std(axis=0)}")
    print(f"    ratio to max|true| = {ratio}")
    print(f"    => effective epsilon = {ratio[0]:.3e} (S), {ratio[1]:.3e} (I), "
          f"{ratio[2]:.3e} (D), {ratio[3]:.3e} (R)")
    print()

    return np.sqrt(np.diag(cov_theta)), s2

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduction of the PIWR result on the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark.

Paper: "Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation
in Epidemic Models" (arXiv:2610.19058), claim C1 / Table 2, row alpha.

The paper's own code is not released, so PIWR is reimplemented from the
equations in sections 2 and 3.2:

  eq. (5)/(28)  SIDR model, linear in theta = (alpha, beta, gamma)
  eq. (12)      x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta with J_j = int_{t0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds
  eq. (13)      cubic-spline (not-a-knot) quadrature, integrated exactly
  eq. (14)      augmented system with x0 as n extra unknowns
  eq. (11)      unit column-norm scaling before the solve
  eq. (16)      SVD least squares, never the normal equations
  R7            compartment-wise noise, std = eps * max_t |x_c(t)|
  R14           errors in percent of the actual value

Usage:
    python reproduce.py            # full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # fast sanity checks only
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import evaluate, piwr, sidr


def log(msg):
    print(msg, flush=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- data
def build_dataset():
    """True trajectory, the DINN benchmark file, and the 1 % noise data."""
    t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
    X_true = sidr.simulate(t)

    # The DINN repo ships the *noise-free* SIDR benchmark; audit its effective
    # noise level so the choice of generator for the 1 % data is documented.
    audit = None
    if os.path.exists(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV):
        d = np.genfromtxt(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV, delimiter=",")
        X_csv = d[1:].T
        cmax = np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
        ratio = (X_csv - X_true).std(axis=0) / cmax
        audit = {
            "file": os.path.relpath(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV, C.WORKSPACE),
            "shape": list(d.shape),
            "t_matches_grid": bool(np.allclose(d[0], t)),
            "effective_epsilon_per_compartment": ratio.tolist(),
            "is_noise_free": bool(np.all(ratio < 1e-4)),
        }

    # R7: 1 % noise, std = eps * max_t |x_c(t)|, independent per compartment/time.
    rng = np.random.default_rng(C.POINT_ESTIMATE_SEED)
    X_noisy = sidr.add_noise(X_true, C.NOISE_EPSILON, rng)
    return t, X_true, X_noisy, audit


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ checks
def matrix_checks(t, X_noisy):
    """Shape / rank / conditioning sanity of the augmented system."""
    W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)
    M, y, J = piwr.build_system(X_noisy, W)
    norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    Ms = M / norms[None, :]
    s = np.linalg.svd(Ms, compute_uv=False)
    return {
        "M_shape": list(M.shape),
        "expected_shape": [C.N_SAMPLES * C.N_STATES, C.N_STATES + 3],
        "J_at_t0_all_zero": bool(np.all(J[0] == 0.0)),
        "min_column_norm": float(norms.min()),
        "rank": int(np.linalg.matrix_rank(Ms)),
        "condition_number_scaled": float(s[0] / s[-1]),
        "singular_values_scaled": s.tolist(),
        "alpha_column_max_abs": float(np.max(np.abs(J[:, :, 0]))),
    }


def noise_scale_check(t, X_true, X_noisy):
    """Verify the injected noise really has std = eps * max_t |x_c| (R7)."""
    cmax = np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
    resid = X_noisy - X_true
    return {
        "epsilon": C.NOISE_EPSILON,
        "max_abs_true_per_compartment": cmax.tolist(),
        "target_noise_std": (C.NOISE_EPSILON * cmax).tolist(),
        "observed_noise_std": resid.std(axis=0).tolist(),
        "observed_over_target": (resid.std(axis=0) / (C.NOISE_EPSILON * cmax)).tolist(),
    }


def regressor_noise_check(t, X_true, X_noisy):
    """How much noise sits in the large-magnitude S-equation regressor.

    The alpha column of M is int S*I/N ds, whose magnitude reaches ~2.7e8 while
    the noise in the sampled I compartment is 1 % of max|I| = 1.3e5, so the
    regressor itself is noisy (errors in variables).  This is intrinsic to
    evaluating the library at the measured states, as the paper does.
    """
    W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)
    Jt = piwr.integrated_library(sidr.library(X_true), W)
    Jn = piwr.integrated_library(sidr.library(X_noisy), W)
    col = 0  # alpha column
    d = Jn[:, :, col] - Jt[:, :, col]
    scale = np.max(np.abs(Jt[:, :, col]))
    return {
        "alpha_column_max_abs": float(scale),
        "regressor_noise_std": float(d.std()),
        "regressor_noise_relative": float(d.std() / scale),
        "note": ("library evaluated on the raw noisy states, no smoothing; "
                 "J is the exact spline integral of the noisy library"),
    }

"""Where does the alpha error at 1% noise come from?

Refit alpha from each single equation block (S, I, D, R) separately and compare
with the full augmented system.  No normal equations are formed anywhere.
"""

import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import piwr, sidr

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
true = np.array([C.TRUE_PARAMS[k] for k in C.PARAM_NAMES])
W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)


def fit_cols(Xn, rows, cols):
    M, y, _ = piwr.build_system(Xn, W)
    M = M[np.ix_(rows, cols)]
    y = y[rows]
    z, _ = piwr.solve(M, y)
    return z


# column layout of M: [x0_S, x0_I, x0_D, x0_R, alpha, beta, gamma]
ALL = np.arange(400)
S_ROWS = np.arange(0, 400, 4)
I_ROWS = np.arange(1, 400, 4)
D_ROWS = np.arange(2, 400, 4)
R_ROWS = np.arange(3, 400, 4)

variants = {
    "full (all 4 equations)": (ALL, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]),
    "S equation only": (S_ROWS, [0, 4]),
    "I equation only": (I_ROWS, [1, 4]),          # beta+gamma not separable here
    "D equation only": (D_ROWS, [2, 6]),          # gamma
    "R equation only": (R_ROWS, [3, 5]),          # beta
}

N = 400
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
res = {k: np.zeros((N, 3)) for k in variants}
for k in range(N):
    Xn = sidr.add_noise(X, C.NOISE_EPSILON, rng)
    for name, (rows, cols) in variants.items():
        z = fit_cols(Xn, rows, cols)
        if name == "S equation only":
            th = np.array([z[1], np.nan, np.nan])
        elif name == "I equation only":
            th = np.array([z[1], np.nan, np.nan])
        elif name == "D equation only":
            th = np.array([np.nan, np.nan, z[1]])
        elif name == "R equation only":
            th = np.array([np.nan, z[1], np.nan])
        else:
            th = z[4:]
        res[name][k] = th

for name in variants:
    a = res[name][:, 0]
    b = res[name][:, 1]
    g = res[name][:, 2]
    print(f"{name:24s} alpha median err {np.nanmedian(100*np.abs(a-true[0])/true[0]):7.4f} %   "
          f"beta {np.nanmedian(100*np.abs(b-true[1])/true[1]) if not np.all(np.isnan(b)) else float('nan'):7.4f} %   "
          f"gamma {np.nanmedian(100*np.abs(g-true[2])/true[2]) if not np.all(np.isnan(g)) else float('nan'):7.4f} %")

# signed bias of the full fit (errors-in-variables attenuation check)
full = res["full (all 4 equations)"]
print()
print("signed mean alpha_hat - alpha:", np.mean(full[:, 0] - true[0]))
print("signed mean beta_hat  - beta :", np.mean(full[:, 1] - true[1]))
print("signed mean gamma_hat - gamma:", np.mean(full[:, 2] - true[2]))
print("std alpha_hat:", np.std(full[:, 0]), " => %.3f %% of alpha" % (100*np.std(full[:,0])/true[0]))

class DINN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, t, S_data, I_data, D_data, R_data): #[t,S,I,D,R]
        super(DINN, self).__init__()
        self.N = 59e6 #population size
        self.t = torch.tensor(t, requires_grad=True)
        self.t_float = self.t.float()
        self.t_batch = torch.reshape(self.t_float, (len(self.t),1)) #reshape for batch 
        self.S = torch.tensor(S_data)

"""Which noise model reproduces the paper's alpha error?

Three candidate models:
  (a) additive, std = eps * max_t|x_c|      -- paper R7 / Nielsen et al. 2025
  (b) additive, std = eps * std(x_c)        -- DINN notebook, commented-out branch
  (c) multiplicative x~ = (1 + eps*xi)*x    -- DINN notebook, active branch
"""

import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import piwr, sidr

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
true = np.array([C.TRUE_PARAMS[k] for k in C.PARAM_NAMES])
eps = C.NOISE_EPSILON
N = 500


def noise_additive_max(X, rng):
    cmax = np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)
    return X + eps * cmax * rng.standard_normal(X.shape)


def noise_additive_std(X, rng):
    cstd = np.std(X, axis=0)
    return X + eps * cstd * rng.standard_normal(X.shape)


def noise_relative(X, rng):
    return (1.0 + eps * rng.standard_normal(X.shape)) * X


models = {
    "(a) additive eps*max|x_c|  [paper R7]": noise_additive_max,
    "(b) additive eps*std(x_c)  [DINN abs]": noise_additive_std,
    "(c) multiplicative (1+eps*xi)*x [DINN]": noise_relative,
}

for name, fn in models.items():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2024)
    errs = np.zeros((N, 3))
    for k in range(N):
        Xn = fn(X, rng)
        th = piwr.fit(Xn, t)["theta_hat"]
        errs[k] = 100 * np.abs(th - true) / true
    a = errs[:, 0]
    med_params = np.median(errs, axis=1)
    print(f"{name}")
    print(f"    alpha : median {np.median(a):7.4f} %  mean {a.mean():7.4f}  "
          f"q05 {np.percentile(a,5):7.4f}  q95 {np.percentile(a,95):7.4f}")
    print(f"    beta  : median {np.median(errs[:,1]):7.4f} %   "
          f"gamma : median {np.median(errs[:,2]):7.4f} %")
    print(f"    median-over-params (Table 3 comparable): median {np.median(med_params):7.4f} %")
    print(f"    fraction of draws with alpha err <= 0.124 %: {np.mean(a <= 0.124):.4f}")
    print()

def add_noise(X, epsilon, rng):
    """Compartment-wise Gaussian noise (R7 / section 5.1).

    x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + epsilon * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi_i,  xi_i ~ N(0, 1)

    This is the convention the paper states for its synthetic benchmarks and
    attributes to Nielsen et al. (2025).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    scale = epsilon * np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)
    return X + rng.standard_normal(X.shape) * scale


def add_noise_dinn_relative(X, epsilon, rng):
    """Noise convention of the DINN benchmark generator, verbatim.

    repo/Experiments/noise/covid_noise_0.01.ipynb, cell 1 (the *active* branch;
    the "absolute noise" branch above it is commented out):

        noise = 0.01
        S_noise = (1 + noise * np.random.randn(1, n)[0]) * sidr_data[1]
        I_noise = (1 + noise * np.random.randn(1, n)[0]) * sidr_data[2]
        D_noise = (1 + noise * np.random.randn(1, n)[0]) * sidr_data[3]
        R_noise = (1 + noise * np.random.randn(1, n)[0]) * sidr_data[4]

    i.e. epsilon enters as a *per-point multiplicative* factor
    x~_c(t_i) = (1 + epsilon * xi_i) * x_c(t_i), one independent standard normal
    per compartment and time point, drawn compartment by compartment in the
    order S, I, D, R.

    Note: cell 0 of that notebook calls ``torch.manual_seed(1234)``, which seeds
    PyTorch and *not* NumPy, so ``np.random.randn`` there is unseeded and the
    notebook's own draw is not reproducible.  We therefore use an explicit,
    documented NumPy seed and draw the four compartments in the notebook's order
    so the random stream matches its structure.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    out = np.empty_like(X)
    for c in range(X.shape[1]):  # S, I, D, R -- the notebook's draw order
        xi = rng.standard_normal(X.shape[0])
        out[:, c] = (1.0 + epsilon * xi) * X[:, c]
    return out


def add_noise_dinn_absolute(X, epsilon, rng):
    """The DINN notebook's *commented-out* "absolute noise" branch, verbatim:

        S_noise = sidr_data[1] + noise * np.std(sidr_data[1]) * randn(...)

    i.e. x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + epsilon * std_t(x_c) * xi_i.  Kept for
    completeness; it is not the branch the notebook executes.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    scale = epsilon * np.std(X, axis=0)
    return X + rng.standard_normal(X.shape) * scale

    "dinn_absolute_std": add_noise_dinn_absolute,

"""Verify predicted_se against a well-conditioned reference (unscaled SVD)."""

import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import piwr, sidr, evaluate

t = np.linspace(0.0, C.T_END, C.N_SAMPLES)
X = sidr.simulate(t)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
Xn = sidr.add_noise(X, C.NOISE_EPSILON, rng)

se_scaled, s2 = evaluate.predicted_se(Xn, t)

# reference: SVD of the UNSCALED matrix (no normal equations, no rcond truncation)
W = piwr.quadrature_weights(t)
M, y, _ = piwr.build_system(Xn, W)
U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(M, full_matrices=False)
z, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(M, y, rcond=None)
r = y - M @ z
s2u = float(r @ r) / (M.shape[0] - M.shape[1])
cov = s2u * (Vt.T @ np.diag(1.0 / s**2) @ Vt)
se_unscaled = np.sqrt(np.diag(cov))[4:]

print("cond(M)          =", s[0] / s[-1])
print("cond(M^T M)      =", (s[0] / s[-1])**2, " -> pinv(M^T M) truncates here")
print("s2 (scaled route)=", s2)
print("s2 (unscaled)    =", s2u)
print("SE scaled  route :", se_scaled)
print("SE unscaled SVD  :", se_unscaled)
print("max rel diff     :", np.max(np.abs(se_scaled - se_unscaled) / se_unscaled))
print()
print("beta SE == gamma SE exactly?", se_scaled[1] == se_scaled[2])
print("  -> the D-block rows are [e_D | 0,0,int I] and the R-block rows are")
print("     [e_R | 0,int I,0]; the x0 columns are orthogonal indicators, so the")
print("     design treats beta and gamma symmetrically.  It is an exact identity")
print("     of the design matrix, not copied bookkeeping.")
print()
# empirical check of the SE over many realizations
errs, thetas = evaluate.sweep(t, X, 1000, 0)
print("empirical std(alpha_hat) over 1000 draws :", thetas[:, 0].std())
print("predicted SE(alpha)                      :", se_scaled[0])
print("ratio empirical/predicted                :", thetas[:, 0].std() / se_scaled[0])
print("  -> the OLS standard error assumes noise-free regressors, but the library")
print("     is evaluated on the noisy states (errors in variables), so it under-")
print("     estimates the true spread.  This is why the paper needs conformal")
print("     calibration and the residual-adaptive RACC layer.")

## What was built

`python reproduce.py` runs end-to-end in ~3 s and writes `results/metrics.json`. It reimplements **PIWR from the paper's equations** (the authors released no code for their method — the linked repo is the DINN *baseline*):

- `src/sidr.py` — SIDR vector field (eq. 5/28), LSODA at rtol=atol=1e-10 (R15), the R7 compartment-wise noise model, and the DINN notebook's multiplicative noise convention.
- `src/piwr.py` — library A(x,t) with no unknowns (R1), cubic-spline not-a-knot quadrature integrated exactly to every t_j via grid-only weights (R2/R3), the augmented system with x₀ as 4 extra unknowns (R4), unit-column-norm scaling (R6), and an SVD least-squares solve that never forms the normal equations (R5).

## Headline (C1)

`alpha_rel_error_pct = 1.0780 %` — α̂ = 0.188941 vs α = 0.191, from a single fixed-seed (seed 0) 1 % noise draw. **`within_tolerance: false`** (band [0.1116, 0.1364]).

## Why it misses, and why that is honest

The paper never states which noise realization produced its Table 2 entry, so an exact match is not reproducible. The diagnostics show the gap is a **draw, not a bug**:

- Over 1,000 independent R7 draws: median 0.711 %, IQR [0.337, 1.213], 5–95 % range 0.065–2.056 %. The paper's 0.124 % is an ordinary ~10th-percentile draw.
- The paper's own Table 3 median-over-parameters figure for PIWR at 1 % noise is 0.46 %; we obtain **0.4945 %** — a close match on the statistic the paper actually defines.
- Noiseless check: α error **3.79e-5 %** (paper: 1.05e-4 %), same order — confirms the quadrature/augmented-LS machinery is correct.
- Timing: **0.56 ms** median per fit (paper: 0.21 ms), same order.

## Two findings worth flagging

1. **The repo's SIDR CSVs are noise-free.** `repo/Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv` is *byte-identical* to `repo/Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv` (effective ε ≈ 1e-8, pure solver round-off). The 1 % noise is generated *inside* `covid_noise_0.01.ipynb` cell 1 with an **unseeded** `np.random.randn` (`torch.manual_seed(1234)` does not seed NumPy), so the paper's exact draw is unrecoverable. Both files are audited in the metrics.
2. **The OLS standard error under-predicts the spread by 7.5×.** The library is evaluated on the noisy states (errors-in-variables), so eq. (17)'s σ̂_α = 0.139 % of α while the empirical std is 1.04 %. This is precisely why the paper needs conformal calibration and the residual-adaptive RACC layer. (I also verified the β SE == γ SE equality is an exact design-matrix identity, not a bookkeeping bug, and that `predicted_se` agrees with an unscaled-SVD reference to 1e-7.)

No seed, noise convention, or row scaling was chosen to move the headline toward the target. The DINN multiplicative-noise convention is reported as a diagnostic only (median 0.270 %).

## Not done

A2 (row-scaling Dₙ selection) was not wired in — only 1 step of budget remained and I would not risk breaking the working entrypoint. An earlier diagnostic already ran it: Dₙ=diag(1/max|x_c|) gave a *worse* median (0.569 % vs 0.511 %), so the paper's Dₙ=Iₙ rule that is currently wired in is also the better choice.

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

audit_summary: The code faithfully implements the PIWR point-estimation pipeline needed for C1: parameter-linear SIDR library, not-a-knot cubic-spline quadrature of the integrated weak form, joint x0 unknowns, column-scaled SVD least squares, LSODA 1e-10 data generation, and R7 compartment-wise noise. The executed target is the same dataset, split, method and metric as C1; the reported 1.078% alpha error is computed from a single seeded 1% noise draw, not copied. It misses the 0.124% band (0.1116-0.1364), but the 1,000-draw diagnostic (median 0.711%, IQR 0.337-1.213) shows the target is an unexceptional draw, and the noiseless check and Table-3-style median-over-parameters (0.495% vs 0.46%) support correctness. The DINN repo's SIDR 1% CSV is actually noise-free and the notebook's NumPy draw is unseeded, so the exact paper realization cannot be recovered; the gap is driven by randomness, missing exact noisy data, and paper underspecification (A1, A2, A4, A6, A8, A18), not by a wrong experiment or hard-coded result. Only C1's point-estimate path is exercised; conformal/RACC requirements R8-R11 are not implemented, and the timing diagnostic times the solve only, so the other claims are not fully audited. No scale-down was used for the target run.

requirement_check.evidence: src/sidr.py builds the SIDR library A(x,t) with only S,I,N; theta=(alpha,beta,gamma) are the physical parameters (identity h for SIDR), so A contains no unknowns.
src/piwr.py build_system constructs x_j = x0 + J_j theta from the integrated library J; no differentiation of noisy data is used.
src/piwr.py quadrature_weights uses scipy CubicSpline with not-a-knot end conditions on the sample grid and exact antiderivative; check_piwr.py verifies the weights against direct spline integration.
build_system pads M with an identity block for x0; fit returns x0_hat jointly with theta_hat.
solve uses numpy.linalg.lstsq on the column-scaled matrix (SVD-based), and the normal equations are not formed for the headline solve.
solve scales columns to unit norm before the solve and rescales coefficients back; column_scaling=True by default.
sidr.add_noise implements x~_c(t_i)=x_c(t_i)+epsilon*max_t|x_c(t)|*xi_i with independent standard normals; the headline draw uses this function on the true trajectory.
No conformal calibration prior box or calibration problem generation is implemented; C1 is a point estimate, so this part is outside the executed path.
No split-conformal maximum-normalized score or simultaneous quantile intervals are implemented.
No PIWR-RACC residual-adaptive h=1+R/Rbar tuning layer is implemented.
No 999 calibration problems or alpha=0.1 conformal calibration run is implemented.

evaluate.predicted_se computes OLS standard errors for theta (identity h for SIDR), but no explicit delta-method propagation through a non-identity h is implemented and no conformal intervals are produced.
config.py uses N=59e6, x0=(N-1,1,0,0), alpha=0.191, beta=0.05, gamma=0.0294, and 100 linspace samples on [0,500] days.
evaluate.pct_error computes 100*abs(hat-true)/abs(true); summarise reports the median over estimated parameters.
src/sidr.py simulate calls solve_ivp with LSODA and rtol=atol=1e-10.
